label: D2 phase (reached-state step); magnitude higher for S2
explanation: Fires on every D2 step (the step where the reached state is shown) and essentially nowhere else: 46 stray GO activations, none at D1. phase == D2 gives F1 ~1.0 on dev. Because this is just a phase detector, its information is in the magnitude. Magnitude is ordered mainly by the reached state: S2 fills the top two activation quartiles (state==S2 covers 99-100% of quartiles 3-4 but only 1-7% of quartiles 1-2). Within a state, choosing a2 also raises it: from the example windows, S2 common (a2) is about 0.86-1.0 of max, S2 rare (a1) about 0.8-0.93, S1 rare (a2) about 0.76-0.88, S1 common (a1) about 0.6-0.79. Only uses observed inputs (state and last action at D2).

issues: None of the factual claims failed. phase == D2 scores precision 1.0, recall 0.9999 and F1 0.99994 on dev and test, with mass recall 0.99999. No step fires at D1 (0 on both splits). GO strays number 46 on dev and 51 on test and carry 0.0% of the activation mass.
The test misses are tiny GO activations (0.00-0.13 of max), mostly a2 choices, and there are 0 false positives. This is negligible residue, not a systematic class.
The S2 magnitude claim holds on test: D2 & state==S2 covers quartiles [0.013, 0.071, 0.993, 1.0].

The within-state ordering was unscored in the original, so I checked it on test by quartile coverage. S1/a1 covers [0.96, 0.38, 0, 0], S1/a2 [0.03, 0.55, 0.007, 0], S2/a1 [0.01, 0.06, 0.38, 0.02] and S2/a2 [0.002, 0.01, 0.61, 0.98]. This confirms S1 common < S1 rare < S2 rare < S2 common, so 'a2 raises activation within state' holds. Magnitude is roughly a sum of a state effect (larger) and an action effect.
The label does not overclaim. The binary predicate is phase only, and the magnitude statements are presented as secondary, which my scores support.
